studies.outcome: shrunk lambda 0.822646 using only training; test per-race Brier 0.133218->0.132209; paired race CI improvement [0.000636,0.001399]; favorite PL 66.96%, actual 57.12%, shrunk 58.63%

studies.title: Pre-specified conditions to use 6–10 earlier starts in M3 only for selected horses
studies.population: 2024 338R train and 2025-26/10/04 569R diagnostics; H005 paired full-field score cohort; 2024-26 already previously explored
studies.intervention: Retain alpha=0.8 decayed last5 gap input except per-horse gate: return same surface ±200m (old6-10>=2 recent5<=1); stable frontness (last10 same surface>=8, |front_new5-old5|<=.12); recent5 gap SD>=.5s; change only pred_gap

studies.title: Observed course-specific middle-pace lull mechanics from 200m race laps
studies.population: 35,857 CP932 JRA lap rows; 5,368 result race keys; 4,912 exact date+venue+race name matches; 1,670 turf 3win+ 12-18 1200/1600/1800/2000 clean laps; 631 Tokyo/Nakayama major profiles, 2016-2026/10/04
studies.question: Do course structure and race distance materially alter mid-race pace lull, rather than using venue-average performance as horse ability?
studies.definition: For >=1600m, mid segment fourth 200m fraction to before final600m >= early2 nonstarting 200m and final600m mean each by >=0.3 sec/200m; 1200m is NA, not a negative class
studies.findings: Tokyo turf1800 41/80=51.25% vs Nakayama turf1800 4/65=6.15%, difference 45.10pp bootstrap95%CI 32.69..57.21pp; Tokyo/Nakayama 1600 37.6%/15.1%; 2000 40.3%/39.4%; threshold 0.2/.5 and graded/good-going checks same direction
studies.modelImpact: none; target race laps known after race, do not insert as forward predictors
studies.next: H008-B: frozen as-of course profile probability vs ability/M3-conditioned horse response, proper holdout, no lane/gps inference
studies.caveat: Not causal effect of turn count alone: track grade, course layout, distance, field and race-day pace composition confounded; no before-start horse aptitude test
